_comentario: How the kiosk UNDERSTANDS what people say in Brazilian Portuguese (registro/Conversacion). What the kiosk SAYS is not here: it is in the catalog (context «totem», i18n/ba_pt-BR.ts). The word lists are compared against the speech-to-text output once flattened (lowercase, without the accents in «aplanar» and with punctuation as spaces): «não» and «nao», «está» and «esta», «é» and «e» are the same word once flattened, so a bare «é» is never a yes (it would match the connector «e»). They can be written with accents: they are flattened when the file is read. A phrase is several words separated by one space; a hyphen is a space too («e-mail» → «e mail»). What the kiosk says has to be answerable with these lists: the catalog confirmation («Diga “sim, está correto” ou “não, está incorreto”», «sim, está tudo correto» / «não, tem algo errado») with the ones in «respuestas», and the dictated email example («joao ponto silva arroba gmail ponto com») with the ones in «correo». See docs/desarrollo/I18N.md, «Tótem: datos del idioma».

aplanar._comentario: Letter (UTF-8) → what it becomes when flattened. Anything not listed here that is not ASCII is dropped. A space: taken as a separator. The typographic apostrophe becomes the plain one. Guillemets, curly quotes and dashes are spaces.

numeros._comentario: Numbers said in words. «regla» «es» (Conversacion.cpp, grupo()), which fits Portuguese: the hundred is a word of its own («duzentos», «trezentas»; «cem» is in «centenasSolas» because it goes alone: 100, while «cento» takes a rest: «cento e vinte»), followed or not by «e» («conectoresCentena») and 1..99; a ten («trinta») followed or not by the connector «e» and a unit 1..9 («trinta e cinco»); or a unit (0 to 19, one word each: «dezesseis»). «mil» multiplies what comes before (or 1) and adds; the «e» after it is filler («mil e duzentos» = 1200); «millon» multiplies everything before. «ninguno» counts as zero. «meia» is 6 because that is how Brazilians say a six in a phone number («meia meia» = 66). LIMITS: a ten said without «e» («vinte um») gives 20 and 1 as two numbers (in a phone they come out as «201»); «meia» is always 6, even where it means half; feminine forms («duas», «duzentas») are listed one by one. «digitos»: how each digit 0..9 is said, to read back a phone or an email (not flattened).

respuestas._comentario: Yes or no. First «noSabe» (neither yes nor no: ask again) and «noFrases» (a no even if it has a yes inside: «não está certo»); then, if one of «si» or of «no» appears (and not both), that one. The first of each list is the one used when the model answers with a boolean. A bare «é» or «tá» is not here: flattened, «é» is the connector «e», and «tá» is in too many sentences.

_comentarioListas: cancelar, repetir and saltear: «exactas» = the whole utterance is that; «contiene» = it appears in the utterance (as whole words).

correo._comentario: The dictated email. «signos»: what is said instead of a sign, in order (multi-word phrases are replaced first, then single words). «noSonDigitos»: units of «numeros» that are not turned into a digit («uma» is an article; «um» stays a digit because people dictate «um» for 1, and so does «meia»). «antes» and «despues»: what is said before the email («meu e-mail é») and after («obrigado»), which is removed. «terminaciones»: domain endings that, standing alone after the at sign, take a dot («gmail com» → gmail.com, «uol com br» → uol.com.br). «dominios»: a domain said without its ending that is completed. «decir»: how each sign is read back aloud.

telefono._comentario: «mas»: what is said for the + of the country code (only at the start); «decirMas», how it is read back. «repetir»: «duplo cinco» = 55, «triplo zero» = 000 (rare in Brazil, but harmless). «grupo»: how many digits are read and shown together (the first group takes the remainder: a mobile with area code, 11 98765 4321, is shown as 119 8765 4321).

nombre._comentario: «antes»: what is said before the name, in order (the first one that matches at the start is removed, and again, until none is left). «despues»: at the end. «noEmpiezaCon»: if the utterance starts like this, it is not a name («não quero»). «particulas»: lowercase in the middle of a name («Maria da Silva», «João dos Santos», «Ludwig van Beethoven»).

opciones._comentario: Picking an option by its order: «orden» has, for the first, the second…, how it is named; «ultima», the last one.

_comentarioEtiqueta: etiquetaEnMinuscula: a field label said in the middle of a sentence starts lowercase («Anotei e-mail…»; an acronym like «CPF» stays).
